*Published 2 November 2026. Every number here was measured that day:
sih-br-mcp 1.8.1 on the public endpoint, microdatasus 3.0.0 with dplyr 1.2.1
and R 4.6.1 on Windows, PySUS 2.11.7 with Python 3.13 on Linux, over a
residential connection in Brazil. The scripts are in
[`scripts/comparativo/`](https://github.com/SidneyBissoli/sih-br-mcp/tree/master/scripts/comparativo)
of the sih-br-mcp repository; nothing is illustrative. The same comparison,
as a product page:
[sih.sidneybissoli.com/vs-microdatasus-pysus](https://sih.sidneybissoli.com/vs-microdatasus-pysus).*

If you work with Brazilian public hospital admissions — SIH/SUS, the AIH
records DATASUS publishes every month — you almost certainly reach the data
through one of two packages: [microdatasus](https://github.com/rfsaldanha/microdatasus),
by Raphael Saldanha, in R, or [PySUS](https://github.com/AlertaDengue/PySUS),
by the AlertaDengue team, in Python. Both download and decode the
**microdata**: one record per admission.
[sih-br-mcp](https://sih.sidneybissoli.com) is mine and sits one layer up: an
MCP server that answers the **aggregate question** inside an AI assistant
(Claude, ChatGPT, any MCP client) from pre-built cubes, with provenance in
every answer.

They are tools for different jobs, which is exactly why it is worth putting
all three in front of the same question.

## The question, and why it needs 432 files

> How many pneumonia admissions (ICD-10 J12–J18) did residents of Espírito
> Santo have in 2024, and how many deaths?

It looks like one file. DATASUS publishes SIH as one file per **hospital
state** and **billing month** (the month the AIH was billed, not the month
of admission). The question is by state of **residence** and **admission
date**. Two consequences:

- A resident of Espírito Santo admitted in Minas Gerais is in Minas Gerais's
  file.
- An admission in December 2024 may be billed in March 2025; the four
  following billing months close 99.7–99.9% of a year.

The honest answer from microdata: 27 states × 16 billing months (2024-01 to
2025-04) = **432 files, 1,358 MiB of `.dbc`, 18,863,265 records**.

The natural shortcut, reading only Espírito Santo's 16 files (30 MiB), gives
**13,097** admissions. It misses 208: residents admitted in Minas Gerais
(102), Rio de Janeiro (83) and elsewhere. Small (1.6%), and exactly the kind
of difference nobody notices.

## Three ways

| | Admissions | Deaths | Downloaded | Time |
|:--|--:|--:|:--|--:|
| **sih-br-mcp** 1.8.1 | 13,305 | 1,250 | 21 KB response | 0.9 s |
| microdatasus 3.0.0 | 13,305 | 1,250 | 432 files, 1,358 MiB | 40.6 min |
| PySUS 2.11.7, `group="RD"` | 9,135 | 760 | 345 of 432 files | 59.4 min\* |

\* On Linux under WSL, reading and writing the Windows disk: not comparable
with microdatasus's time.

microdatasus and sih-br-mcp reach **the same number, group by group**: J12
461, J13 37, J14 1, J15 3,648, J16 265, J17 100, J18 8,793. That is neither
coincidence nor anyone's merit: sih-br-mcp's cubes are built from a 1:1
Parquet mirror of the same `.dbc` files, over the same billing-month window.
What differs is **where the work happens**. With microdata, on your machine,
for every question. With sih-br-mcp, once, when the cubes are built; the
question only reads the result.

PySUS fell short for a reason that gets its own section below.

### microdatasus (R)

One file at a time: binding all 432 does not fit in memory.

```r
library(microdatasus)
library(dplyr)

ufs   <- c("AC", "AL", "AM", "AP", "BA", "CE", "DF", "ES", "GO", "MA", "MG", "MS", "MT", "PA",
           "PB", "PE", "PI", "PR", "RJ", "RN", "RO", "RR", "RS", "SC", "SE", "SP", "TO")
comps <- seq(as.Date("2024-01-01"), as.Date("2025-04-01"), by = "month")

pneu <- list()
for (d in as.list(comps)) for (uf in ufs) {
  y <- as.integer(format(d, "%Y")); m <- as.integer(format(d, "%m"))
  rd <- fetch_datasus(year_start = y, month_start = m, year_end = y, month_end = m,
                      uf = uf, information_system = "SIH-RD",
                      vars = c("MUNIC_RES", "DT_INTER", "DIAG_PRINC", "MORTE"))
  pneu[[length(pneu) + 1]] <- rd |>
    filter(substr(MUNIC_RES, 1, 2) == "32",                     # lives in ES
           substr(DT_INTER, 1, 4) == "2024",                    # admitted in 2024
           substr(DIAG_PRINC, 1, 3) %in% sprintf("J%02d", 12:18))
}
bind_rows(pneu) |> summarise(admissions = n(), deaths = sum(MORTE == "1"))
#>   admissions deaths
#> 1      13305   1250
```

432 files, no errors, 40.6 minutes. `fetch_datasus()`'s `vars =` helps: only
four columns stay in memory. Note `MORTE == "1"`: `fetch_datasus()` returns
everything as character, and that is what you compare — after
`process_sih()`, the code becomes `"Sim"`/`"Não"`.

### PySUS (Python)

```python
import pandas as pd
import pysus

ufs = "AC AL AM AP BA CE DF ES GO MA MG MS MT PA PB PE PI PR RJ RN RO RR RS SC SE SP TO".split()
comps = [(2024, m) for m in range(1, 13)] + [(2025, m) for m in range(1, 5)]
pneumonia = {f"J{n}" for n in range(12, 19)}

parts = []
for y, m in comps:
    for uf in ufs:
        rd = pysus.ftp.sih(state=uf, year=y, month=m, group="RD", as_dataframe=True)
        if rd.empty:
            continue
        parts.append(rd[rd["MUNIC_RES"].str[:2].eq("32")
                        & rd["DT_INTER"].str[:4].eq("2024")
                        & rd["DIAG_PRINC"].str[:3].isin(pneumonia)])
pneu = pd.concat(parts)
len(pneu)
#> 9135
```

### sih-br-mcp (inside the assistant)

The question goes in plain language. The assistant picks the tool, and the
call it makes is this:

```
get_hospitalizations {
  "uf": ["ES"], "year": [2024], "cid_chapter": [10], "group_by": ["cid_group"]
}
```

The answer carries one row per ICD group (J12 to J18 add up to 13,305
admissions and 1,250 deaths) and a provenance block saying where each number
came from: the billing months read (2024-01 to 2025-04, all 27 file states),
the mirror's vintage, the MD5 of every source `.dbc` and the formal DATASUS
citation. First call in the session, 0.9 s; the second, 0.7 s.

## The trap in the middle: PySUS 2.11.7 and the files without a group

With `group="RD"`, the loop above returned **9,135** admissions, not 13,305 —
31% fewer, with no error and no warning.

PySUS 2.x does not list the DATASUS FTP on each call: it queries its own
catalog (a DuckDB database downloaded on first use) pointing to Parquet
copies of the files. In that catalog, **4,526 of the 10,946 SIH RD files have
no group**. A `group="RD"` query filters by group and does not see them. In
this question's window that is **87 of 432 files** — including 7 of
Espírito Santo's own 16 months (Jan, Feb, Mar, Jul and Nov 2024; Jan and Apr
2025) — and the pneumonia admissions inside them add up to **4,170**. The
arithmetic closes: 9,135 + 4,170 = 13,305.

Calling **without** `group` reaches those files, together with the month's
other groups (ER, RJ and SP), which you then drop by name. On Windows there
is a second defect, upstream of that one: the catalog returns `WindowsPath`
objects, their `str()` comes out with backslashes, and a prefix check written
with forward slashes discards them all. The SIH calls came back empty, and so
did the file listings for SIM and SINASC. That one had already been
[reported](https://github.com/AlertaDengue/PySUS/issues/372) and is fixed in
the code since 30 October
([PR #374](https://github.com/AlertaDengue/PySUS/pull/374)), awaiting the
next release.

The missing-group one I [reported the same
day](https://github.com/AlertaDengue/PySUS/issues/380). It is the kind of
defect fixed in an afternoon. Meanwhile, anyone using PySUS 2.11 for SIH
should check **how many files came back**, not only how many rows.

## Volume, in numbers

| | Size |
|:--|:--|
| Raw SIH-RD microdata, 1992–2026, in the mirror | 23.86 GiB, 11,211 files, 432,173,746 records |
| Everything sih-br-mcp's cube channel publishes | 1.63 GiB |
| This post's question | 1,358 MiB from microdata; 21 KB from sih-br-mcp |
| Admissions, days, spending and deaths per year, 1992–2025 | 420,107,114 admissions, one call under 1 s |

## What sih-br-mcp does not do

- **Individual records.** The cubes are aggregates; no AIH can be recovered.
- **Variables the cubes do not carry**: procedure performed, facility (CNES),
  admission type, secondary diagnosis.
- **Other DATASUS systems**: SIM, SINASC, SIA, SINAN, CNES.
- **What DATASUS published today.** The vintage is the mirror's, and every
  answer says which.

For all of that, use microdatasus or PySUS.

## Which one

- **Aggregate question, auditable answer, inside the assistant**:
  sih-br-mcp.
- **Record-level data, variables outside the cubes, other systems, in R**:
  microdatasus (and [read.dbc](https://cran.r-project.org/package=read.dbc)
  if you only need to open the `.dbc`).
- **The same, in Python**: PySUS, checking how many files came back.
- **To check sih-br-mcp**: redo the count from microdata, as this post did. A
  difference is a bug; [open an
  issue](https://github.com/SidneyBissoli/sih-br-mcp/issues) with the slice.

The three complement more than they compete. sih-br-mcp exists only because
the microdata is open and because microdatasus and PySUS showed, for years,
what can be done with it. Thanks to Raphael Saldanha and the PySUS team.
